study.briefTitle: A Phase II Trial of Triapine (NSC #663249) in Combination With Gemcitabine as Second Line Treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

criteria.text: Patients must have histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); cytology alone is not acceptable
Patients must have progressive or recurrent NSCLC
must have failed one and only one prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease
patients must not have received prior gemcitabine chemotherapy
Patients must have measurable disease, as defined by RECIST, within 4 weeks prior to registration
Patients must have an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Bilirubin < 1.5 x upper limit of normal
AST (SGOT) < 3 x upper limit of normal
Serum creatinine =< 1.5 mg/dL, or calculated creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min
Absolute granulocyte count >= 1500/mm3
Hemoglobin >= 9 g/L
Platelet count >= 100,000/mm^3
Patients must have completed any radiation therapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration
Patients must have completed prior cytotoxic chemotherapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration
have recovered from adverse effects from the chemotherapy to =< Grade 1, or baseline
Patients with brain metastases which have been treated are eligible if the patient is > 3 weeks post completion of treatment for their brain metastases, and patient is neurologically stable
patients with previous brain metastases who have not yet received therapy specifically intended for their brain metastases are not eligible to enroll in this protocol
Life expectancy greater than 3 months
Pregnant women are excluded from this study
breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with Triapine®
a negative serum pregnancy test is required within 14 days of study entry

women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation
HIV-positive patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy are excluded from the study
Patients must not have an active second malignancy

Patients must not have, at the time of registration, uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements
a history of myocardial infarction within the prior 6 months
symptomatic congestive heart failure
unstable angina pectoris
cardiac arrhythmia requiring medical intervention (with the exception of chronic, stable, asymptomatic atrial fibrillation)
pulmonary disease requiring oxygen
Patients must not have dementia or active psychosis
Patients must not have used any investigational agent in the month before study enrollment
Patients must not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to Triapine® or other agents used in this study
Patients must not have a clinical history of G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency
persons at high risk for this condition (patients of African, Asian, or Mediterranean origin/ancestry) must undergo specific clinical testing at protocol entry for this condition
patients testing positive for G6PD deficiency are excluded from protocol entry

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "A Phase II Trial of Triapine (NSC #663249) in Combination With Gemcitabine as Second Line Treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be eligible, the lung cancer diagnosis must be confirmed by looking at tissue samples under a microscope (biopsy). Has your doctor confirmed your NSCLC diagnosis this way, rather than just using cells from fluid or sputum?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my doctor confirmed it with a biopsy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has your doctor told you that your non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has gotten worse (progressive) or come back (recurrent) after previous treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: It's recurrent: it came back after treatment, and it's progressing.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received exactly one prior chemotherapy treatment for your advanced lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I've had one chemo regimen since it spread, and it stopped working.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received a chemotherapy drug called gemcitabine before?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've not had gemcitabine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any imaging scans (like a CT or PET scan) in the last 4 weeks to check if your cancer is still visible and measurable?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I need to take that back: gemcitabine was part of my chemo. I haven't had any scans in the last 4 weeks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: To clarify, have you had any recent imaging scans (like a CT or PET scan) in the last 4 weeks that showed your cancer was still visible and measurable? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure. I haven't had any scans in the last 4 weeks, so I don't know if they showed the cancer was visible and measurable.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To check your ECOG performance status, how would you describe your ability to carry out daily activities? An ECOG score of 0 or 1 means you are fully active or restricted only in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory. If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm fully active and can do everything I used to do, just a bit slower. I'd say my ECOG score is 0.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you completed any radiation therapy at least 3 weeks before you would register for this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I finished radiation about two months ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you completed any prior chemotherapy treatments at least 3 weeks before you would register for this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: The radiation finished eight days ago, not two months. My last chemo was more than five weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you recovered from side effects of your last chemotherapy to Grade 1 (mild symptoms) or back to your normal baseline? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the specific grade. I'm feeling better, but I don't know the medical details of my recovery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: To clarify, are your side effects from the last chemo now mild (like a headache or mild nausea) or gone, and are you back to your usual daily routine?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm feeling better and back to my usual daily routine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been treated for brain metastases? If so, was it more than 3 weeks ago, and have you been stable with no new or worsening neurological symptoms (like headaches, vision changes, or weakness) since then?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been treated for brain metastases.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for more than 3 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I expect to live for more than 3 months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant, or do you think there is any chance you could be pregnant?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No. I'm a man, so not pregnant.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Not breastfeeding, being a man.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a blood pregnancy test within the last 14 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had a blood pregnancy test. I'm a man, so that wouldn't apply to me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to use an effective birth control method (like condoms or hormonal birth control) or practice abstinence during the study and for a period after it ends?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'll use condoms from before I start and all through the study.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with HIV and received combination antiretroviral therapy (a mix of medicines used to treat HIV)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with HIV or taken those medicines.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a second type of cancer that is currently active or being treated?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have another active cancer. Just the lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any ongoing infections (like a fever or active cold) or any mental health conditions that might make it hard to follow the study rules?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any ongoing infections or mental health conditions that would interfere.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a heart attack (myocardial infarction) in the last 6 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had a heart attack in the last 6 months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with symptomatic congestive heart failure, which is a condition where the heart doesn't pump blood as well as it should and causes symptoms like shortness of breath or swelling?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with congestive heart failure.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with unstable angina pectoris, which is chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart that occurs at rest or with minimal exertion?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with unstable angina.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an irregular heartbeat (cardiac arrhythmia) that required medical treatment, such as medication, a procedure, or hospitalization? Please note that this does not include chronic, stable, and symptom-free atrial fibrillation.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had an irregular heartbeat that needed treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently use supplemental oxygen to help with breathing due to a lung condition?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't use supplemental oxygen.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with dementia or active psychosis?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with dementia or active psychosis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you taken part in any other clinical trials or received any investigational medications in the past month?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes. Three weeks ago I finished a study of an experimental drug for my arthritis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to Triapine or any other medicines with a similar chemical or biologic makeup?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I got hives from a chemo drug years ago. No idea whether it's anything like this one.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: To clarify, do you know if the chemo drug that caused your hives has a similar chemical makeup to Triapine, or are you unsure?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure. I don't know if that old chemo drug is chemically similar to Triapine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with G6PD deficiency, which is a genetic condition affecting red blood cells?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: G6PD deficiency? No, I don't have that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.
